name: phase1_low_end
description: Is the step between HW 0 and HW 1 a discontinuity, or is the curve just
super-linear across the first few bits?
phase1_hamming_weight fits dP = 0.362 + 0.0500*HW watts (R^2 = 0.974) but
dP(0) is zero by construction, so the line extrapolates to a +362 mW
intercept that the data cannot contain. phase1_nonzero_baseline then ruled
out the dangerous explanation -- there is no fixed per-contrast offset, the
intercept of measured-on-predicted is +14 +/- 23 mW -- so the step belongs
to the operand. It did not settle *where* in the operand range it lives.
Two loose ends from that session point the same way. Its contrasts touching
the lowest weights came in above prediction (+57 mW at z=+2.7, +115 mW at
z=+2.5, both positive), and its internal chain implies hw01 -> hw04 =
+0.217 W where the sweep's own points put that step at +0.043 W. A factor
of five is not a rounding disagreement. Either the sweep's HW 1-4 points are
too close together to trust at one pattern each, or the curve really does
climb steeply over the first few bits and then flattens to 50 mW/bit.
So: sample the region the sweep skipped. HW 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6, two bit
patterns each, every run contrasted against the same all-zero baseline the
sweep used, at driver settings identical to it so the points can be pooled.
Predictions, against measured dP:
HW   line (0.362 + 0.05*HW)   sweep measured   chain reading
A flat-ish set of points near the line says the sweep was right and the
step is a genuine discontinuity at zero -- all-zero data is anomalously
cheap to move, and every dP in the depth table is an overestimate by a
constant. Points climbing steeply from HW 1 to HW 4 and then rejoining the
line says the transition is smooth and there is no discontinuity to explain.
Two patterns per weight because bit placement is worth 0.04-0.16 W at equal
weight elsewhere in this data, which is the same size as the effect being
resolved here; one pattern per point cannot tell placement from shape.
hw01_a, hw04_a and hw04_b repeat the sweep's own operands exactly, so they
double as a cross-session reproduction. anchor_hw16 is the session anchor.
Read with analysis.hwfit; note it will fit a slope over a range where the
hypothesis is that a single slope does not fit, so read the per-point means.
